cultivar: Fengqing large-leaf and other Yunnan big-leaf (assamica) cultivars
processing: Fully oxidised: a bud with one or two leaves is withered, rolled and straightened rather than twisted, then oxidised and dried; the straight shaping is about appearance and even extraction.
harvest_season: Spring (March–April) for the best lots; autumn pickings are common and cheaper.
appearance_dry: Long, slim, straight dark strands with gold only at the tip, glossy and intact.
appearance_liquor: Clear bright red with an orange rim.
appearance_wet: Long copper-red leaves with golden buds, opened flat and even.
taste_profile: Malt and cocoa up front, honey and sweet potato through the middle, with more body and a brisker, slightly peppery finish than the all-bud styles.

brewing.notes: Do not pack the gaiwan: the straight leaves take up space before they open. 90–95 °C, short early steeps; makes a strong, milk-friendly pot at 3 g per 250 ml for 3 minutes.

vintage_note: Sold by the current year's harvest, spring first and autumn as the cheaper option; good for a year or two in a sealed bag but not meant for ageing.
description:
Pine Needle Dian Hong, Song Zhen, is the everyday workhorse of the Fengqing straight-leaf styles: a bud with one or two leaves shaped into long, slim, straight strands that are darker than Golden Needle and carry gold only at the tip. It gives you most of what people like in Yunnan black – malt, honey, sweet potato – with more body and a lower price than the all-bud teas.

The leaf is withered, rolled and straightened rather than twisted, then oxidised and dried; the straight shaping is purely about appearance and even extraction. Having real leaves alongside the buds means more tannin and more aroma than Jin Ya, so the liquor is a proper red rather than amber and the cup has some grip.

Expect malt and cocoa first, honey and sweet potato through the middle, and a brisk, slightly peppery finish; it goes six or seven steeps in a gaiwan and makes a strong, milk-friendly pot. It is hard to brew badly: 90–95 °C water, short early steeps, and do not pack the gaiwan because the straight leaves take up space before they open.

It is sold by the current spring harvest, mostly from Fengqing and the rest of Lincang, with autumn lots common and cheaper. Look for long, intact, glossy strands with golden tips and a sweet, malty dry aroma; lots of broken pieces mean rough handling or old stock.

It is the Dian Hong to drink daily, and the right one to compare against Golden Needle if you want to feel what the leaf adds to the bud.
